item.title: Jamie Overton runs riot with five-wicket haul as Australia register lowest-ever home T20I total
item.description: Australia suffered a major batting collapse in the third T20I against England at the Gabba in Brisbane on Friday, registering their lowest-ever T20I total on home soil. With the five-match series level at 1-1, England captain Harry Brook won the toss and elected to bowl first. The decision worked perfectly as England's bowlers dismantled the Australian batting line-up, bundling out the hosts for just 108 in 16.5 overs. Jamie Overton's five-wicket haul demolishes Australia Jamie Overton was the pick of the bowlers, claiming a sensational five-wicket haul for just 12 runs. Liam Dawson provided excellent support with three wickets for 16 runs, while Sam Curran chipped in with one wicket. Jake Fraser-McGurk provided Australia with an aggressive start, scoring 22 off 11 deliveries, while Sam Harper contributed 26 off 14 balls. However, England struck at regular intervals to prevent the hosts from building any meaningful partnerships. Dawson dismissed Australian captain Mitchell Marsh for 11 before Overton took control of the innings. The pacer removed Tim David, Joel Davies, Nikhil Chaudhary, Ben Dwarshuis and other key batters to complete his five-wicket haul. Nikhil Chaudhary managed 19 runs, while Mitchell Owen scored 16, but neither could prevent Australia's collapse. Sam Curran eventually wrapped up the innings, leaving England with a target of 109 runs. Australia's lowest T20I totals at home 108 vs ENG, Brisbane, 2026* 111 vs NZ, Sydney, 2022 119 vs IND, Carrara, 2025 127 vs PAK, Melbourne, 2010 The 108-run total is also Australia's second-lowest score in T20I cricket against England, behind their 79 all out at Southampton in 2005. It is also the lowest first-innings total recorded at the Gabba in T20 cricket. England will now look to chase down the target of 109 runs and take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series.

item.description: Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Tom Pelissero gives play-by-play of what led to Aaron Rodgers’ failed ‘ultimatum’ before scorched-earth exit appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers had an eventful day at the beginning of the week, and it ended with Aaron Rodgers being released by the team. It all started with Rodgers being benched in the middle of the night , and the next day, he went on the Pat McAfee Show and aired out head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers went on to say that McCarthy would be sleeping in meetings, and sometimes he was a no-show. He also mentioned that at halftime during their game against the Philadelphia Eagles, McCarthy broke down the huddle with “1-2-3 Packers.” Maybe an hour later, Rodgers was released. Everybody wants to know what led up to the tension between Rodgers and the Steelers, and according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, it started on Tuesday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Rogers went to McCarthy on Tuesday to demand more changes, including to the play-calling process,” Pelissero said. “McCarthy was open to it, but the feedback he’d gotten from some coaches, and some in the locker room, was that’s not what they wanted. Those discussions ended with an ultimatum for Rogers. Run things my way, or I quit. And the Steelers called his bluff. Tom Pelissero: "(Aaron) Rodgers went to (Mike) McCarthy on Tuesday to demand more changes, including to the play-calling process… Those discussions ended with an ultimatum from Rodgers: 'Run things my way, or I quit.' And the Steelers called his bluff." pic.twitter.com/HxiN4GHJuK — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 26, 2026 “But Tuesday afternoon, McCarthy had decided he wanted to start Mason Rudolph on Friday against the Denver Broncos, and GM Omar Khan called Rogers directly to let him know about the change.” It looked like the Steelers weren’t going for anything that Rodgers was saying, and it led to the big blow-up. It also seems as if the organization is fully behind McCarthy, and they still have a chance to make the playoffs, as they’re currently 6-4. As for Rodgers, there’s a possibility he’s done playing football, unless a team decides to pick him up at some point during the end of the season. item.title: Mikel Arteta demands scoring spree from goal-shy Arsenal
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta is pictured ahead of the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium. (is associated with: «Mikel Arteta demands scoring spree from goal-shy Arsenal») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Mikel Arteta wants his Arsenal players to find their sense of fun by snapping out of the team’s goal-shy streak and hitting “five, six or seven”. The champions have not scored more than two goals in a Premier League match since beating promoted Coventry 3-0 on the opening day of the season and have drawn their last two fixtures. They host Manchester City at the Emirates on Sunday looking to move nine points clear of Enzo Maresca’s side, having failed to win any of their three games against City in all competitions last season. It would be a fine time for the Gunners to summon up a ruthless streak in front of goal and potentially end City’s title challenge before the end of November. “I prefer to win by five or six or seven, for sure,” said Arteta. “I’m going to enjoy the game much more, especially the last few minutes. The boys are going to have more fun. “Scoring goals, ultimately what it creates is good feeling, joy, happiness around the stands. It’s the most important thing in football.” Arsenal lead the table by six points ahead of hosting City but have scored only 17 goals in their 11 league games so far, making them just the seventh-highest scorers in the division. They are currently being outscored by eighth-placed Chelsea and have netted only two more goals than Ipswich, who are 16th. A defensive record of seven goals against has been their foundation as they seek to retain the title for the first time since 1935, and even if the goals do not flow, Arteta wants his players to relish the challenge. “The fun is being there on the grass and training,” he said. “If that’s not fun I think we have a problem. Then within that you can find moments, synergies and be a bit creative. Not to make it every single day the same. But I think the boys love to train and love to play, which is what you need.” Arteta was unable to say whether David Raya will be fit to return on Sunday having missed Tuesday’s 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League. It could mean a first league start of the season for Kepa Arrizabalaga, who came on when Raya was forced off injured against Newcastle on Saturday. It would also be a first appearance against City for Kepa since his errors led to two goals in March’s Carabao Cup final defeat. “We still have a few hours for the game,” said Arteta. “We’re just trying to get everybody back. They’re all training. “Every player has the same mindset, everyone want to be available, wants to be in the best possible condition. “The experience that Kepa has is already incredible, in the teams he’s been involved, the squads he’s been involved, the trophies that he’s won.” Last season’s meeting with City at the Emirates ended level after Gabriel Martinelli scored

item.title: 'Haaland is a winner:' Maresca not worried about Man City star’s form
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester City's Erling Haaland appeals to officials during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Manchester City and Napoli at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «'Haaland is a winner:' Maresca not worried about Man City star’s form») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Enzo Maresca has no concerns about the form or demeanour of Erling Haaland amid Manchester City’s slump in form. The City boss also believes the Norwegian’s mood may have been influenced by a number of debatable refereeing decisions in recent games. City have won just one of their last seven fixtures in all competitions and Haaland had not scored in his last three outings for the club. The Norwegian also offered a blunt assessment of City’s performance after their midweek draw with Napoli in the Champions League, when he often cut a frustrated figure. “Erling is a winner player,” Maresca said. “It’s normal that he’s not happy when he’s not winning games but don’t forget a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch. “Erling is upset just like I am upset. It’s not a sprint, it’s a marathon. We are building something for the future. “I think he is gesticulating in the same way when we were winning games and he was not receiving balls. Erling is a (number) nine and the nines live day by day for goals and winning games. If they don’t score or win games they are upset. “I don’t think that affects his game. I don’t see any problem at all with Erling.” Haaland was aggrieved during last weekend’s draw against Fulham when he had a goal disallowed for a foul on goalkeeper Bernd Leno. The striker poked home at the second attempt after Leno failed to gather his initial shot cleanly, but the German was deemed to have the ball under control when Haaland made contact. Maresca can understand why Haaland would feel frustrated in such circumstances and believes it was merely the latest in a line of harsh decisions against City. The Italian said: “I can see that, to be honest. I can see also more things in the last three, four, five games, probably since, the international break, that happened. “I’ve never seen in my life a player touch the ball with both arms – no penalty, for instance against Brighton, (Lewis) Dunk. Or the other one that was like volleyball, or the last one against Fulham. “If you just stop (the footage) when the goalkeeper has the ball, it looks like (a foul), but the dynamic he is not catching the ball. Even the keeper does not believe that he was. “But again, because the referee is there, they decide, so we need to adapt.” City face champions and leaders Arsenal in Sunday in a game they can ill afford to lose if they are to keep pace at the top of the table. Maresca insists City will head to the Emirates Stadium without trepidation. He said: “We have already shown this season that we are able to win important games, to win away. item.title: Sharks make flurry of roster moves ahead of Golden Knights clash
item.description: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Sharks make flurry of roster moves ahead of Golden Knights clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After missing out on the Stanley Cup Playoffs by just four points in 2025-26, the San Jose Sharks have disappointed this year, winning just 11 of their first 27 games and sitting outside a postseason berth the day after Thanksgiving. A 7-0 beatdown at the hands of the Anaheim Ducks on Wednesday night added insult to injury for the reeling franchise. The club is now six points back in the Western Conference wild-card race. The Sharks made a few changes at the back of their roster ahead of another Pacific Division tilt on Friday, this time against the Vegas Golden Knights. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The [Sharks] have recalled F Cam Lund and D Luca Cagnoni from the San Jose Barracuda,” the team announced. “F Brett Leason and D Libor Hajek have been re-assigned to the Barracuda.” This is the first recall of the season for Lund, who began the 2026-27 campaign on injured reserve before being activated and sent down to the American Hockey League in October. The 22-year-old has fared well since returning, chipping in a goal and seven assists over 13 AHL games. He has appeared in 11 NHL games, all during the 2024-25 season, recording two goals and three points while averaging 11:30 of ice time per contest. Cagnoni will be more familiar to Sharks fans. He made the team straight out of training camp and was playing in a top-four role early in the season, including getting reps with the first power-play unit. He ended up with two points and a minus-nine rating in nine games before being demoted. He’s fared better with the Barracuda, managing four goals and seven points in 12 contests. With Lund and Cagnoni joining the NHL roster, Leason and Hajek will return to the Barracuda. The former appeared in two games with San Jose, failing to record a point. Overall, he’s managed 25 goals and 29 assists in 228 career NHL games across six seasons. He has eight points in 14 games with the Barracuda in 2026-27. As for Hajek, he hasn’t played an NHL game since 2022-23. He spent two seasons playing in his native Czechia and has two points in 15 games with the Barracuda this season. Following the four moves, San Jose’s active roster remains full with 23 players. Puck drops on Sharks-Golden Knights just past 4 p.m. ET Friday at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. item.title: "I couldn't see myself anywhere else" – El Mala loyal to Köln despite prior Dortmund links
item.description: "I couldn't see myself anywhere else" – El Mala loyal to Köln despite prior Dortmund links Last summer, Said El Mala decided to remain at 1.FC Köln, extending his contract by one year, through 2031, which surprised the masses. "I feel the responsibility, the pressure, and the expectations that the people in Cologne have of me. But that’s a good thing for me. "Being pushed a little always helps me move forward; it usually brings out an even better performance. "Plus, I have plenty of people around me who support me through it all, so I’m quite relaxed about it," the Köln star told Kicker.de. Prior to his contract extension, El Mala was the subject of persistent interest from Borussia Dortmund at the time. BVB reportedly produced an offer of around €50million — a fee deemed not enough by Köln, and therefore the move did not materialize. But did El Mala himself even want to join Dortmund? When asked why he stayed in Cologne this summer, El Mala replied: "We were actually in talks with FC the whole time. It’s no secret that I received offers, which I did listen to. “But I couldn't see myself anywhere else,” the 20-year-old claimed, which somewhat goes against his previous media statements. At the height of the summer transfer drama, various media reports had suggested he was very keen on a move to Dortmund. Whether his comments reflect his genuine stance remains an open question. One thing is clear – a move away is off the table for now.

item.title: 'We show class on the way out': Terry Bradshaw rips Aaron Rodgers over Steelers exit
item.description: Terry Bradshaw spent 14 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and he wasn’t a fan of how Aaron Rodgers left the organization. The Steelers benched Rodgers on Tuesday, and less than 24 hours later, he went scorched earth on head coach Mike McCarthy during a surprise appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, prompting the team to release him and igniting one of the biggest stories in the league this year. Rodgers has already been getting a lot of criticism, with former Packers teammates James Jones and T.J. Lang both ripping the quarterback, and CBS’ Nate Burleson calling him out for dodging accountability. On Fox’s Thanksgiving pregame show, Bradshaw piled on to the criticism as he defended McCarthy and the Steelers’ organization. “They’re a classy bunch, classy organization. Mike McCarthy and I have been friends for years. Classy man. I don’t know all the details,” Bradshaw said of the Rooney family and the Steelers. Terry Bradshaw, a real Pittsburgh Steeler, spitting facts about Aaron Rodgers: https://t.co/pO2SYWWOk1 — Cory Tucek (@Cory_Tucek) November 26, 2026 Terry Bradshaw then made it clear that Aaron Rodgers’ outburst didn’t surprise him. “You know what? I’m just gonna tell you how I feel right now. I’m sorry that Aaron Rodgers had to do this. I’m sorry that he had to go public with all his gripes and complaints,” Bradshaw said. “Am I surprised? Absolutely not. To my opinion, he’s a strange guy anyway.” The four-time Super Bowl champion argued that players should never turn on their own organization on the way out. “And the one thing you don’t do, all of us athletes up here, including you, none of us turn on our teammates. We don’t turn on our coaching staff. We don’t turn on our ownership. We show class on the way out,” Bradshaw said. “Aaron Rodgers didn’t do that.” Terry Bradshaw also took a shot at Rodgers’ retirement plans. Rodgers has said that once his playing career is over, “it’s Keyser Söze, and you won’t see me.” “And one thing I’m reminded of, he said, ‘When I’m through playing here in Pittsburgh, I’ll disappear, and you’ll never hear or see from me again,'” Bradshaw said. “And I hope this is one time he’s telling the truth.” The post Terry Bradshaw hopes Aaron Rodgers fulfills his promise and disappears in retirement appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Is This The Real Reason the Steelers Cut Rodgers Before Black Friday?
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph (2) hands off to running back Lew Nichols III (31) in the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 10 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Monday, Nov. 16, 2026. The Bengals improved to 7-2 on the season with a 38-18 win over the Steelers. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph as their starting quarterback for the Friday game against the Denver Broncos, according to a report. The move places Rudolph in a high-pressure role as he attempts to stabilize an offense that has lost its last two games. The Steelers enter the contest with a 6-4 record, while the Broncos arrive in Pittsburgh with an 8-2 record and six straight wins. Rudolph has faced difficult moments throughout his nine-year career, and he views this situation as another chapter to overcome. He acknowledged that the rapid change from backup to starter creates an awkward environment for the team. Despite the chaos surrounding the quarterback room, he believes the players must focus on the game rather than the off-field drama. The game is scheduled for 3 p.m. ET at Acrisure Stadium and will be broadcast on Amazon Prime. A Difficult Week for the Franchise The last few days have been chaotic for the Pittsburgh organization . Head coach Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers had a falling-out that led to the release of the four-time MVP. After being benched, Rodgers appeared on “The Pat McAfee Show” to express his frustration with the coaching staff and the team’s direction. This public conflict has drawn significant attention away from the football itself. Rudolph was not aware he would start until the night before the announcement. By the time Rudolph spoke to the media, the narrative had already shifted to the fallout between Rodgers and the coaching staff. The situation has placed the players in a unique position where they must support their coach while managing the departure of a future Hall of Famer. The team has since held a meeting to address the issues and move forward. They now face a steep challenge with only seven games remaining in the regular season. If the season ended today, the Steelers would qualify as the seventh seed in the playoffs. The pressure is on to bounce back against a Denver team that has dominated its recent opponents. The coaching staff must now prove that they can lead the team to victory without their most high-profile player. Rudolph’s History of Adversity Mason Rudolph has encountered significant obstacles throughout his time in the NFL. The Steelers selected Oklahoma State’s third-round pick in the 2018 draft. His career has included being benched for an undrafted rookie and suffering a severe injury in which his helmet was ripped off by Myles Garrett. He also spent a season with the Tennessee Titans before returning to Pittsburgh in 2025. These experiences have prepared him for the instability of the current situation.

item.title: Rishabh Pant record in away Tests: Is he India's best bet in SENA and overseas conditions?
item.description: Rishabh Pant record in away Tests: Is he India's best bet in SENA and overseas conditions? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Rishabh Pant has built a strong case as India's most dependable overseas batter. His away numbers hold up well and include a rare milestone from Wellington. The figures also show how he compares with India's other leading batters since 2018. MORE: What is Last Man Stands game in NZ cricket? Pant plays amateur game What is Rishabh Pant's record in away Tests? List by country in table Rishabh Pant's record in away Tests is the first thing that comes up whenever India's fans and selectors discuss who can hold the batting together on a tough tour, and the numbers from the last eight years back up much of that talk. The wicketkeeper-batter is the highest-scoring designated keeper in away Test history, and his century in Wellington this month has made the debate over his place in India's overseas plans even louder. Across 36 away Tests and 63 innings, Pant has piled up 2,617 runs at an average of 43.61, with seven hundreds and 11 half-centuries to go with them. More than two-thirds of his 53 Tests have been played outside India, which makes it all the more notable that his away average sits only 1.19 below his overall career average of 44.80. item.title: Calgary Flames Have a Former 50-Goal Junior Scorer Who Deserves a Bigger Opportunity
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Brennan Othmann scored his first goal of the season and added an assist in the Calgary Flames’ 6-3 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Wednesday. He registered five shots on goal in just 9:40 of ice time without playing a second on the power play. The 23-year-old is averaging just 9:21 through eight games this season, and it’s worth seeing what he could produce if Ryan Huska gave him more minutes alongside some of the Flames’ skilled forwards. The New York Rangers selected Othmann 16th overall in the 2021 NHL Draft. The following season, he scored 50 goals and recorded 97 points in 66 games with the Flint Firebirds of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL), adding 24 points in 19 playoff games. He won two World Junior gold medals with Canada and an OHL championship with the Peterborough Petes. His shot was one of his biggest strengths entering the draft, and he had no problem playing physically despite being one of his team’s most productive offensive players. Othmann Could Score at the Professional Level, Too Othmann scored 21 goals and recorded 49 points in 67 games with the Hartford Wolf Pack as a rookie in 2023-24, finishing second on the team in scoring and earning an American Hockey League (AHL) All-Star selection. Despite missing 10 weeks with an upper-body injury the following season, Othmann scored 12 goals in 27 AHL games and made 22 NHL appearances. That’s 33 goals in his first 94 AHL games. His production dropped last season, as he recorded 16 points in 26 games with Hartford before the Flames acquired him in exchange for Jacob Battaglia in March. He recorded seven points in 14 games with the Calgary Wranglers and three points in 19 NHL games between the two organizations. The Flames signed him to a one-year, two-way contract worth $975,000 in September. Flames Should Give Othmann Some Power-Play Time According to the AHL’s official statistics , Othmann tied Josh Doan for the rookie lead with 10 power-play goals in 2023-24 and led all rookies with 17 power-play assists. More than half of his points that season came on the man advantage, yet he’s averaging just nine seconds of power-play time per game with the Flames this season. Calgary has the NHL’s fifth-ranked power play at 25.8%, but with injuries forcing Huska to move players around , there’s room to experiment. Giving Othmann some of the minutes Ryan Strome received on the second unit Wednesday could be worth trying if Yegor Sharangovich can handle the faceoff responsibilities. The Flames have already seen what some of their younger forwards can produce with more responsibility . Othmann’s physical game makes him a useful option on the fourth line, but he’s scored at every level below the NHL. He might never become a top-six NHL forward, but playing nine minutes a night without regular power-play opportunities isn’t going to tell the Flames much about whether he can. Gabe Perreault became the latest Rangers player to land on IR following that game; the 21-year-old forward is out 4-6 weeks with a lower-body injury . Perreault joins a long list of Rangers on injured reserve, including forwards Pavel Dorofeyev, Oliver Bjorkstrand, Joe Veleno, and defenseman Alberts Smits. Star goaltender Igor Shesterkin is on season-ending injured reserve. To date, the Rangers have 98 man-games lost to injury already this season, a number that will only increase in the coming weeks with so many players out longer-term. There is a sliver of hope that Dorofeyev, who’s missed three games with a lower-body injury, may return Friday after practicing Thursday, but that feels more unlikely than likely. The Rangers recalled forward Juuso Parssinen from Hartford of the American Hockey League on Thanksgiving Day. No matter who plays or not, the Rangers must find a way to dial up some offense against the Blackhawks (9-14-2), who are the third-worst defensive team in the NHL statistically, allowing an average of 3.84 goals per game. item.title: Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal after disappointing start to WSL season
item.description: Renee Slegers has left her role as head coach of Arsenal following a difficult start to the Women’s Super League season for the north London club. The Gunners occupy sixth place in the WSL standings, sitting 12 points behind leaders Chelsea after 11 matches, and remain winless at home in the league this term. The Dutch manager assumed the role from Jonas Eidevall, initially on an interim basis, two years ago before guiding Arsenal to Champions League glory in May 2025. A statement on arsenal.com read: "We can confirm Renee Slegers has left her position as head coach of our women’s first team by mutual consent. "Renee departs following a disappointing start to the 2026-27 season, with assistant coach Aaron D’Antino also leaving the club. Slegers won the Champions League with Arsenal last year (Reuters) "The process of appointing a successor is under way and we will update in due course. Assistant coach Melissa Clarke-Reed will take charge of the team in the interim period. "Everyone at Arsenal would like to thank Renee and Aaron for their contributions to the club and wish them every success in their future careers." Pressure had been mounting on Slegers, particularly with Arsenal struggling to convert in front of goal, and her final match ended in a goalless draw against West Ham last Sunday. Gunners director of women’s football Clare Wheatley said: "It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renee, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here. "In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal, with close support from Aaron. "After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level and change is necessary." Arsenal have two weeks until their next fixture due to the international break, with England set to face Ukraine in a two-legged playoff as Sarina Wiegman’s side aim to secure their place at next year’s World Cup. Once the international break finishes, Arsenal will return to action without Slegers when they travel to Everton on 11 December.

It was followed by a new long-term contract for the teenager on Tuesday, which is understood to run until 2031, and ahead of Sunday’s trip to Sunderland De Zerbi stressed the importance of keeping hold of him. “It’s great news for us, the extension of his contract, because if you see other big teams, big clubs, they are losing young talent in the same situations,” De Zerbi said. “We have to say thanks to the club, because I think it was an important step for us, for the pitch, for the football, but also for the fans, because I think we gave a great signal with this extension of the contract. “And if the agent of Luca, if the family of Luca, accept to stay and to extend the contract, it’s because they believe in the Tottenham project. De Zerbi added: “You have to analyse many things. “I think he is ready to play because he is a mature guy, he has the personality to play in every stadium, every game, but we have to analyse everything he has done this week. “The debut in the first XI, the goal, the assist, the extension of his contract. Everything is for the best. For us, for him, for the club.” De Zerbi used Dejan Kulusevski as an example for Williams-Barnett to follow and the Sweden playmaker could start one of Tottenham’s three matches over the next week after a 17-month absence with a serious knee injury. De Zerbi said: “I don’t know, 50 days, 60 days, 80 days, I don’t know. When he comes back I think he will be crucial for us for the last step of the season.”

item.title: Dan Evans to compete in controversial Gazprom-backed exhibition tournament
item.description: Retired British tennis player Dan Evans is in the line-up for a highly controversial exhibition tournament which is sponsored by Russian energy giant Gazprom . Gazprom is majority state-owned and has been sanctioned by the UK government for its role in funding Russia’s war in Ukraine, with a 2025 statement saying its profits were “lining Putin’s war chest and facilitating the war”. The company sponsors the annual Northern Palmyra Trophies exhibition, which is held this year from 27-29 November in St Petersburg and features 12 current or former tennis players. A spokesperson for the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport told The Independent : “Our position remains that we strongly advise British athletes not to travel to Russia to participate in sports events while the illegal invasion of Ukraine continues.” Russia has not held any official ATP or WTA Tour events since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and Russian and Belarusian players cannot represent their country, instead competing as neutral athletes. However, exhibitions are not covered by the rules governing Tour events and players are free to play in such tournaments on Russian soil. Evans, who retired at Wimbledon this year, has not commented on his decision to take part in the event. The Northern Palmyra Trophies sees two teams face off in a mix of singles and doubles matches, with Evans drawn against world No 11, Russia’s Diana Shnaider, in a Battle of the Sexes-style clash. Frenchmen Adrian Mannarino and Corentin Moutet are also in the line-up, which primarily consists of Russian or Russian-born players. Top-100 players Anastasia Potapova , Kamilla Rakhimova, and Yulia Putintseva , who were all born in Russia, are competing, as is the retired former world No 13 Elena Vesnina . Potapova and Rakhimova have both switched nationality since the war began, with the former now representing Austria and the latter Uzbekistan. Putintseva has represented Kazakhstan since 2012. Russian 17-year-old Anna Pushkareva, compatriot Karen Khachanov , retired Serbian player Jakno Tipsarevic and Kazakhstan’s Alexander Bublik complete the line-up. Former US Open champion Daniil Medvedev competed last year but is absent for 2026. The Netherlands’ Tallon Griekspoor, who is in a relationship with Potapova, sparked a diplomatic incident when he decided to play in last year’s tournament. Dutch Foreign Minister David van Weel issued a public statement urging him to withdraw, to no avail: “It is not forbidden to participate in tournaments in Russia, but I appeal to him not to do so where possible and to look at the moral aspects.” The Russian embassy said it was “deeply concerned” by the “pressure” put on Griekspoor.

The dilemma between Endrick and Gonzalo Garcia went on for long, and eventually it was the Spaniard who decided to move on in his own accord, starting a new journey in the Premier League. Gonzalo Garcia reflects on Real Madrid stint Speaking to the media in a recent interview, the former Real Madrid striker opened up on his time at the club, his eventual departure and even his adaptation to English football. He began by explaining how playing for Los Blancos was easier said than done, and the massive expectation that comes with defending that crest. One of Real Madrid’s academy standouts. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “I’m not going to lie to you, it’s not easy at all. I am a Madrid player, having managed to be in the first team of Real Madrid and having the great luck of being able to be part of that team was and continues to be a dream,” he began, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo . “When summer arrives and they raise the possibility of having to leave, obviously you think about it a lot,” he added. The player then elaborated on how former Real Madrid manager Alvaro Arbeloa played a massive role in bringing him to England, saying, “The coach called me, Arbeloa called me, he explained to me the project that was here in Fulham.” “Talking to him, one sees the great ambition that there is in the whole project, to play in the Premier League. Having talked to Álvaro, everything became a little easier,” he added. Arbeloa was critical in helping Gonzalo finalize his departure. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) On the difference in the Premier League Explaining how the Premier League differs from La Liga, and how his adaptation to the new league has been, Garcia said, “The change is quite big, but I think I come very well prepared.” “I have been playing for Real Madrid for twelve years, one in the first team and another eleven in the quarry, and I think there is no better place to learn and raise yourself within the world of football than La Fabrica .” He then explained the difference between the two leagues in terms of the physicality of the play, saying, “It’s a change in style of play, more physical, everything is a little different from Spain, but at the moment I’m happy and adapting little by little.” Finally, Garcia revealed that he still tries and finds the time to watch all the games of his former side. “I try to watch all Madrid’s games, as long as they don’t coincide with mine. The La Masia graduate, currently on loan at Deportivo de A Coruna , will face his parent club this weekend in La Liga, and took time to discuss things related to the Blaugrana ahead of the clash. “I was able to share a few things with the coach that could help us. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
